We need infer circuit topology and resistor values from many node-to-node resistance measurements. Likely it's a complete graph of nodes with resistors in series/parallel? Might be a ladder network? Nodes: A, B, N_b1, N_c1, N_c2, N_c3, N_d1, N_d2, N_d3, X1, X2, X3. Many measurements given. Probably the circuit is a series of resistors between A and B with intermediate nodes? Resistances between A and B is 125. Between A and N_b1 is 11.667, between N_b1 and B is 113.333 (sum 125). So N_b1 is a node on series path from A to B with R_A_Nb1 = 11.667, R_Nb1_B = 113.333. Similarly A to X1 is 6.667, X1 to B is 118.333 (sum 125). So X1 also on series path. So many nodes are points along same series line? Check A to N_c1 =30, B to N_c1 =95 (sum 125). So all nodes lie on same series line between A and B. So the circuit is a simple series resistor chain from A to B with multiple intermediate nodes. Resistances between successive nodes unknown. We have many nodes; need to infer individual segment resistances.

Let order along line from A to B: A - ? - ? - ... - B. The measured resistances from A to each node give distance from A. So we can sort nodes by resistance from A: smallest is X1 6.667, then N_b1 11.667, then X2 25, then N_c1 30, then X3 75, N_c2 40, N_c3 55, N_d1 80, N_d2 90, N_d3 105, B 125.

But note X2 25 less than N_c1 30, okay. N_c2 40, N_c3 55, N_d1 80, N_d2 90, N_d3 105.

Thus the series resistances between consecutive sorted nodes are differences:

A-X1:6.667
X1-N_b1: 11.667-6.667=5.0 (matches measurement N_b1-X1 =5.0)
N_b1-X2:25-11.667=13.333 (matches N_b1-X2 13.333)
X2-N_c1:30-25=5.0 (matches N_c1-X2 5.0)
N_c1-X3:75-30=45.0 (matches N_c1-X3 45.0)
X3-N_c2:40? Wait X3 is 75 > N_c2 40, ordering wrong. Actually N_c2 40 is less than X3 75, so X3 is after N_c3? Let's sort correctly numeric:

Values:
A:0
X1:6.667
N_b1:11.667
X2:25
N_c1:30
N_c2:40
N_c3:55
X3:75
N_d1:80
N_d2:90
N_d3:105
B:125

Now compute differences:

A-X1 6.667
X1-N_b1 5.0 (ok)
N_b1-X2 13.333 (ok)
X2-N_c1 5.0 (ok)
N_c1-N_c2 10.0 (matches N_c1-N_c2 10)
N_c2-N_c3 15.0 (matches)
N_c3-X3 20.0 (matches N_c3-X3 20)
X3-N_d1 5.0 (matches N_d1-X3 5.0)
N_d1-N_d2 10.0 (matches)
N_d2-N_d3 15.0 (matches)
N_d3-B 20.0 (since 125-105=20) matches? Not given but N_d3-B is 20 (given B to N_d3 20). Yes.

Thus consistent series chain.

Thus resistor values are each segment: R_A_X1=6.667, R_X1_Nb1=5, R_Nb1_X2=13.333, R_X2_Nc1=5, R_Nc1_Nc2=10, R_Nc2_Nc3=15, R_Nc3_X3=20, R_X3_Nd1=5, R_Nd1_Nd2=10, R_Nd2_Nd3=15, R_Nd3_B=20.

We need output topology JSON with resistors labeled R1,R2,... and connections list.

Define nodes list: A, X1, N_b1, X2, N_c1, N_c2, N_c3, X3, N_d1, N_d2, N_d3, B.

Assign resistor names sequentially:

R1 between A and X1 =6.667
R2 X1-N_b1 =5
R3 N_b1-X2 =13.333
R4 X2-N_c1 =5
R5 N_c1-N_c2 =10

Return JSON.

Check format: {"resistors": {"R1": 6.667, ...}, "connections": [["A","X1","R1"], ...]}
